title: Clopen restriction to a proper henselian closed fibre
statement: Let (A,I) be a henselian pair [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology], let f:Y → Spec A be proper [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], and let i:Y₀ → Y be the closed fibre in a cartesian square over Spec(A/I) → Spec A. For clopen U,V ⊆ Y, equality i⁻¹(U)=i⁻¹(V) implies U=V. Every clopen V ⊆ Y₀ equals i⁻¹(U) for a clopen U ⊆ Y.

source.place: Lemma 59.91.1, Tag 0A0B, applied to locally constant two-valued functions

proof.text: The quotient spectrum map is a closed immersion, and base change in the given IsPullback square makes i a closed immersion. The isomorphism with the chosen pullback and Mathlib Scheme.Pullback.range_fst identify range(i) with f^{-1}(V(I)); the quotient spectrum range is V(I) by range_comap_of_surjective and Ideal.mk_ker.

source.place: Tag 0A0B, closed fibre; Mathlib AlgebraicGeometry/PullbackCarrier.lean range_fst, and RingTheory/Spectrum/Prime/RingHom.lean range_comap_of_surjective

proof.text: Apply Scheme.Hom.spectralSpace_and_isClosed_and_isConnected_inter: Y is spectral, and every irreducible closed subset meets the closed fibre in a nonempty connected set. In particular this holds for the closure of each singleton.

source.place: Tag 0A0B, proof: spectrality and connectedness of each irreducible closed subset intersected with the closed fibre

proof.text: Every nonempty closed subset C of Y meets range(i): choose x in C, use connectedness (hence nonemptiness) of closure({x}) intersected with the fibre, and use closure({x}) contained in C. If clopens U and V have equal inverse images, a point in U minus V would give a nonempty closed difference meeting range(i), contradicting equality of inverse images. Apply the same argument to V minus U and conclude by subset antisymmetry.

source.place: Elementary consequence of the preceding connectedness assertion, written by M1

proof.text: Use the closed embedding homeomorphism e:Y₀ ≃ range(i) to transport a clopen V to V₁=e(V), whose complement is also closed. Apply TopCat.spectral_closed_clopen_decomposition_lift with Z=range(i) and the connectedness of Z intersected with each point closure. Obtain closed disjoint U,W covering Y and the equality Subtype.val(V₁)=Z intersect U.

source.place: Tag 0CAM, lemma-connected-topological, applied to the closed image of the fibre

proof.text: The disjoint cover gives U=W complement, so U is open as well as closed. For x in Y₀, the intersection identity says i(x) belongs to U precisely when it belongs to Subtype.val(V₁). The latter is equivalent to x belonging to V by e(x)=i(x) and injectivity of i. This proves the required inverse-image equality. The argument includes empty schemes and empty clopens without extra hypotheses.

source.place: Elementary set and homeomorphism calculations, written by M1

proof_origin.place: Tags 0A0B and 0CAM; M1 translates existing Stein connectedness and closed clopen decomposition lifting, with elementary uniqueness and homeomorphism transport

lean.statement:
theorem Scheme.henselian_clopen_restriction
    {A : Type u} [CommRing A] (I : Ideal A) [HenselianRing A I]
    {Y Y₀ : Scheme.{u}} (f : Y ⟶ Spec (.of A)) [IsProper f] (i : Y₀ ⟶ Y)
    (f₀ : Y₀ ⟶ Spec (.of (A ⧸ I)))
    (h : IsPullback i f₀ f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (Ideal.Quotient.mk I)))) :
    (∀ U V : Set Y, IsOpen U ∧ IsClosed U → IsOpen V ∧ IsClosed V →
      i.base ⁻¹' U = i.base ⁻¹' V → U = V) ∧
    (∀ V : Set Y₀, IsOpen V ∧ IsClosed V →
      ∃ U : Set Y, (IsOpen U ∧ IsClosed U) ∧ i.base ⁻¹' U = V)
